chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Jabr, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) used to say, when childbirth was approaching for a woman: 'Remove the women who are in the house, lest one of them be the first to look at the private parts.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for women during childbirth regarding privacy and modesty?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) highlights the Shia emphasis on *satr* (covering) and privacy during the vulnerable state of childbirth. It establishes a specific social protocol to prevent *fitna* (temptation or awkwardness) by ensuring that the first witnesses to the mother’s private parts are limited to appropriate female attendants, thereby preserving dignity and modesty in the domestic sphere.
